decisions.evidence: Putting the six neighbors together, the pattern is mixed but still leans toward option (B). Across all three positive neighbors, the recurring sulfonamide difference is a strong recurring cue, and in the first three comparisons the sulfonamide plus the small QED shifts are the main reasons the query looks more like a skin-reactive molecule. Across the three negative neighbors, the query is consistently larger and more polar in ways that can reduce accessibility, especially the much higher Labute surface area and higher topological polar surface area or N/O burden, but those effects do not fully offset the repeated sulfonamide signal. On balance, the local analog set supports the conclusion that the query causes a skin reaction.
